chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Ya'qubi, from some of his companions, from Abd al-A'la, the client of the family of Sam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him),

who said: A man from the Jews named Sibakht came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said: O Messenger of Allah, I have come to ask you about your Lord. Tell me, where is He? He (peace be upon him) said: He is in every place, yet He is not in any place.

He said: Then how is He? He said: And how should I describe my Lord with kayfiyya, when kayfiyya itself is a creation, and Allah cannot be described through His creation? Then he said to him: What is the proof of Him?

Then the stones upon which [the man] was sitting — nine of them — moved, and they spoke in a clear Arabic tongue: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. Then they returned to their place.
So Sibakht said: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.

key_terms.أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah — the first part of the Islamic declaration of faith, here spoken by inanimate stones as miraculous testimony
key_terms.الْكَيْفُ: al-Kayf — the category of 'how-ness' or modality; in Shi'i kalam, God absolutely transcends this category since it belongs to created things
key_terms.بِلِسَانٍ عَرَبِيٍّ مُبِينٍ: bilisanin 'arabiyyin mubin — in a clear Arabic tongue; an echo of Quran 16:103 and 26:195, underscoring the divine authentication of the Prophet's mission
key_terms.مَخْلُوقٌ: makhluq — created being; used here to establish that kayfiyya (the quality of having a mode) is itself a creature and cannot apply to the Creator

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say when a Jewish man asked how God is described?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates that a Jewish scholar named Sibakht came to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and challenged him with theological questions. When asked about God's location, the Prophet replied that He is everywhere yet transcends all place. When asked about God's nature (kayfiyya), the Prophet said that kayfiyya is itself a creation and Allah cannot be described through His creation — a core Shi'i theological principle. Nine stones then miraculously spoke in Arabic testifying to the faith, and Sibakht converted to Islam.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Al Yaqouby, from one of our companions, from Abdul A’ala, a slave of the family of Saam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A Jew call Sibakht came over to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> and he said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! I came over to ask you<sup>saww</sup> about your<sup>saww</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup>. So if you<sup>saww</sup> were to answer me about what I am asking about (fine), or else I will return’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Ask about whatever you so desire to’.
He said, ‘Where is your<sup>saww</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup>?’ He<sup>azwj</sup> is in every place, and He<sup>azwj</sup> is not enclosed into a thing from the limited place’. He said, ‘And how is He<sup>azwj</sup>?’ He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘And how can I<sup>saww</sup> describe my<sup>saww</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> with the ‘how’, and the ‘how’ is a creation, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> cannot be described by His<sup>azwj</sup> creation’. 
He said, ‘So from where did you<sup>saww</sup> come to know that you<sup>saww</sup> are a Prophet<sup>saww</sup> of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>?’ He (the narrator) said, ‘So there did not remain around him<sup>saww</sup> a tree, nor anything other than that, except that it spoke in clear Arabic language, ‘O Sibakht! He<sup>saww</sup> is Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>!’
So Sibakht said, ‘I have not seen like today, a matter more clear than this’. Then he said, ‘I testify that there is no god except Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and you<sup>saww</sup> are a Rasool<sup>saww</sup> of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Hassan ibn Ali from al-Ba’qubi (Dawud ibn Ali al-Hashimi) from some of our people from ’Abd al-‘Ala’ Mawla Ala Sam from Imam abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said

the following. “A Jew named Sabhut came to the Prophet, (s.a.) and said, “O Messenger of Allah, I have come to ask about your Lord. If you will answer my question it will be fine, otherwise, I will go back.” The Prophet replied, “Ask whatever you like.” He asked, “Where is your Lord?” The Prophet replied, “He is everywhere, but He is not confined in any limited space.”
He asked, “How is He?” The Prophet replied, “How can I describe my Lord by means of conditions that are created. Allah cannot be describe by His creation.”

The Jew asked further, “What is the proof that you are the Messenger of Allah?” The Imam said, “At this point nothing remained around him (the Jew), the stones and all other things, but that they spoke in clear Arabic language, ‘O Sabhut he (Muhammad) is the Messenger of Allah.’
Sabhut said, “I have not seen anything so clearly as this today.” And then he declared, “I testify that there is no god but Allah and you are the Messenger of Allah.”
